sentences.text: According to the revision petitioners, on 30.05.2016 at about 1.00 pm while the deceased Ramu was travelling as a passenger in TNSTC bus from Ramnad, the Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN 65 Z 0907 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the back side of the bus, in which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries on his head and immediately he was taken to Government Hospital, Ramnad and subsequently, died on 22.04.2017.

The revision petitioners, who are the legal heirs of the deceased Ramu filed a claim petition in MCOP.No.206 of 2019 on the file of the Principal District Judge, Ramanathapuram claiming compensation for the death of said Ramu.

During the pendency of the said claim petition, the revision petitioners have taken out an application in I.A.No.241 of 2021 seeking to examine the Government Doctor as witness, who had treated the deceased Ramu after the said accident.
The same was https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis resisted on the side of the respondents.

However, the Tribunal dismissed the said application by stating that though several opportunities were given to the petitioners they have failed to examine additional witnesses and hence, it is only an attempt to drag on the proceedings.
Aggrieved by the same, the present revision is preferred.

3. The learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioners would submit that the said witness is very essential to establish that the deceased Ramu was in continuous treatment after the said accident.
However, the Tribunal, without appreciating the same dismissed the application filed by the petitioners.
Hence, prays for setting aside the impugned order.

4. However, the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent, Insurance Company seriously objected that neither in the petition nor during the examination of the witnesses the petitioners have stated about the continuous treatment of the deceased Ramu in the Government Hospital.
Hence, it is only an attempt to introduce a false case and also to drag on the proceedings.
The Tribunal considering the above rightly dismissed the application, which calls for no interference.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
I have heard the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the materials available on record.

6. The factual matrix of the case is that on 30.05.2016 at about 1.00 pm when the deceased Ramu was travelling as a passenger in TNSTC bus bearing Regn.No.TN65Z0907 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the bus, in which, the deceased Ramu sustained grievous injuries.
He was taken to the Government Hospital at Ramanathapuram for treatment.

Thereafter,
the deceased was in continuos treatment and died on 22.04.2017.

The legal heirs of the deceased,
who are the revision petitioners herein filed the claim petition in MCOP.No.206 of 2019 before the learned Principal District Court, Ramanathapuram for compensation.
Pending claim petition, the revision petitioners have filed reopen petition in I.A.No.241 of 2021 seeking permission of the Court to examine the Government Doctor as witness.
In the said petition it is averred that the deceased Ramu after the alleged accident was taking treatment in Government Hospital at Sivagangai till 08.03.2017 and died thereafter.
However, no post mortem was conducted over the body of the deceased.

Hence, the petitioners would submit that it has become necessary for the petitioners to Selvi vs Jothiammal on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115393499/
2 examine the Doctor, who had treated the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis deceased and to mark the medical records in connection to the said treatment to establish the fact that the deceased Ramu died due to the injuries sustained by him in the said accident.

Though the said application was resisted on the side of the respondent before the Tribunal on the ground that it is only delay in tactics to protract the proceedings and the intended documents are fabricated for the purpose of the case.

The Tribunal based on the averments made in the petition and counter affidavit dismissed the said application by stating that without any iota of evidence the present petition is filed and it is only an attempt to delay the proceedings.
Challenging the same the present revision is preferred.
7. The revision petitioners are none other than the wife and son of the deceased.

The application in I.A.No.241 of 2021 was filed for examining the Government Doctor as witness and mark the medical records connected with the treatment given to the deceased after the alleged accident.
It is not in dispute that that no postmortem was conducted over the body of the deceased.

The specific contention of the petitioners is that since the postmortem was not conducted over the body of the deceased, except by examining the Doctor, who had treated the deceased after the alleged accident and by marking the relevant medical https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis records, the petitioners cannot establish the factum that the death of the deceased was due to the injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident.

There can be no doubt that the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is considered to be the beneficial legislation to protect the rights of the road accident victims and their families and its aim is to provide just compensation to the sufferers.

In the present case, unless the Doctor is examined, who treated the deceased after the alleged accident and the medical records connected to the treatment is before the Court the petitioners cannot establish the cause of the death of the deceased.
Therefore, the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal Judge ought to have considered the same and allowed the application filed by the petitioners.

Therefore, this Court deem it fit in the interest of justice that the order passed in I.A.No.241 of 2021 in MCOP.No.206 of 2019, dated 06.07.2021 on the file of the Principal District Judge, Ramanathapuram is liable to be set aside and accordingly, set aside.
8. In the result, this Civil Revision Petition is allowed.

The learned Principal District Judge,
Ramanathapuram is directed to permit the petitioners to lead additional oral and documentary evidence and also to afford an opportunity to the respondents to cross examine the witnesses https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and test the veracity of the documents and dispose of the case on its own merits untrammeled by any of the observation made by this Court.

Considering the fact that MCOP case is pending from 2019, the learned Principal District Judge, Ramanathapuram is directed to dispose the case within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected Miscellaneous petition is closed.
